question: Verified index-calculus cost over matched Pollard rho (IC / rho), by date landed on main. Below 1 means index calculus is cheaper. The barrier is rho's own cost, 1.
unit_note: Each point is quoted from the frozen result it links, in that result's own unit (Valgrind Ir, S, counted operations, online wall time, or isolated CPU time where marked). Direction against 1 is meaningful only for fully priced ratios; a quotient of incomplete lower bounds is diagnostic even when paired. No value on this page is computed from another.

series.label: Elliptic curve, whole method, cold, one target
series.note: The repository's own definition of faster than rho (AGENTS.md section 2). Hollow markers were later shown to be measured against an unmatched rho and are kept as 'was'.

series.label: Weak elliptic class: cover and decomposition on E(F_p^6)
series.note: Joux-Vitse 2012 reproduced on a genus-3 GHS cover. The ratio falls as p^-1.92 and extrapolates to parity near 2^67 on this weak class (2^65 after F4 is stopped at the Bezout staircase, a 1.61x constant); the isogeny walk to reach it, priced in section 13 at a walk of q/3 steps above rho below p about 8,000, is repriced in section 17: from a curve whose class holds a weak curve it costs about 1% of the route at p = 1,009, and 53-62% of random full-2-torsion curves are in such a class (exact census, p <= 31). Its sieving variant (section 11) measures the crossover with rho at p about 430 (subgroup 2^50) and reads 0.012x at p = 1511. Replaying a recorded F4 trace (section 12) takes another 2.0x off the test: 2.4x at p = 1009, parity extrapolated near 2^62.

points.label: Cover and decomposition, p = 1009 (subgroup 2^57.9), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 8.1x and 10.2x at p = 1009, falling as p^-1.92 +/- 0.12 over five sizes; parity extrapolated near 2^67 (p* about 2,900-3,050), above the harness's 64-bit range. All 10 logarithms recovered.

points.label: Cover and decomposition, F4 stopped at the Bezout staircase, p = 1009 (subgroup 2^57.9), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 5.1x and 6.3x at p = 1009 (8.1x and 10.2x before the stop): F4 stops once the leading monomials leave 64 standard monomials, the partial basis being a Groebner basis already; 1.61x on the test, the same relations from the same residuals, exponent -1.91 +/- 0.12 unchanged; parity extrapolated near 2^65 (p* about 2,300). Class: engineering.

points.label: Sieving variant of the cover route (Joux-Vitse section 3.2), p = 1511 (subgroup 2^61.4), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 0.0122x and 0.0137x at p = 1511 (0.039x and 0.069x at p = 1009; 1.05x and 0.114x at 503; 3.2x and 8.5x at 251; 1,977x and a lower bound above 7,560x at 101): relations from a sieve over the factor base instead of Nagao tests, a measured crossover with rho at p about 430 (subgroup 2^50) where section 6 could only extrapolate one; all ten logarithms above p = 101 recovered. The descent, two Nagao tests, is 46-86 % of the cost from p = 503 up. Class: reproduction of a published route (accounting and engineering), on the weak class only.

points.label: Cover and decomposition, F4 replaying a recorded trace, p = 1009 (subgroup 2^57.9), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 2.98x and 2.40x at p = 1009 (6.3x and 5.1x with the stop alone, 8.1x and 10.2x before it): F4 records, on the first six-quadric system of a size, the pair rows every new pivot is a combination of, and replays them on the rest (no pair selection, no reduction to zero); 2.0x on the test (C_cov 1.6e6, 3.2x against the original), 1,462,000 of 1,516,000 systems replayed, the rest diverged and ran in full; exponent -1.96 +/- 0.11, parity extrapolated near 2^62 (p* about 1,650). Class: engineering.

points.label: Sieving variant, descent replaying the F4 trace, line enumeration of section 14, p = 1511 (subgroup 2^61.4), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 0.0068x and 0.0077x at p = 1511 (0.0075x and 0.0086x before section 14, 0.0122x and 0.0137x before the traced descent): the lines of every B are found from a lazy factorisation (a distinct-degree group split only when a line needs part of it, Cantor-Zassenhaus on the Frobenius columns already computed, x^p by shift and square), 2,600 multiplications per B against 4,200; C_rel at m = 9 falls 1.30-1.35x, S/rho 6-20 % at p = 503-1511 (the descent is the larger term); the same relations from the same B's. Class: engineering.

points.label: Sieving variant at the arithmetic's limit, p = 1,823 (subgroup 2^63.0), best of two seeds; twenty-prime census
points.detail: S/rho 0.0030x and 0.0037x at p = 1,823 and 0.0037x and 0.0047x at p = 1,777 (pooled rho; rho measured by distinguished points at 1,777 in section 16), the largest sizes the 64-bit mod-l arithmetic allows (l below 2^63). A census of one instance on each of ten primes near 500 and ten near 1,000 (all solved) reads 0.04-0.67x and 0.008-0.032x: the spread between instances is the factor base, not the prime, and the crossover from the band means is p about 333 (subgroup 2^48), inside the registered band. Class: measurement.

points.label: Isogeny walk to the weak class priced inside the route (section 17): p = 1,009 (subgroup 2^57.9), walk about 1% of the route for a curve whose class holds a weak curve
points.detail: The walk of section 13 rebuilt: Legendre-form 2-isogeny steps at 2,300-4,500 F_p multiplications per curve met (246x below section 13's 2,3-step), breadth-first enumeration of 2-isogeny components, 3/5/7-isogeny jumps, one point count per walk. From a curve whose isogeny class holds a weak curve (start 8 moves from one), every walk succeeds after a median of 3-16 curves and costs 0.0002x rho at p = 1,009 (0.0038x at 251, 0.0027x at 503), so the route reads 0.021x with the walk inside it and still crosses rho near p about 333-371; a start 64 moves away costs up to 40x more and is still below rho from p = 23. The reach is the new fact: an exact census of every weak curve's class at p <= 31 puts 53-62% of random full-2-torsion curves in a class that holds a weak curve and the rest in one that holds none, where no walk helps; from random starts the walk succeeds 20-54% of the time (p = 7-101), its failures being exact closures with no weak curve. Section 13's 'q/3 steps, above rho below p about 8,000' is superseded. Class: engineering (the step) and accounting (reach and price).

points.label: Cover route end to end from a curve that is not weak (section 18): p = 1,511 (subgroup 2^61.4), 4 seeds
points.detail: The first whole-method run from a non-weak curve: a challenge C isogenous to a weak curve, the walk back to a weak curve, G and Q transported along it, the model change onto the cover form, the sieved route, and verification [d]G=Q on C. 32 of 32 runs across p=251,503,1009,1511 recovered the scalar and verified on C. The walk, transport and model change are under 1% of the cost (E2); the crossover survives (E3), end-to-end S/rho 0.0049-0.019 at p=1511 and 0.035-0.082 at p=1009 for 8 moves off the weak locus. The reach is still the limit: C is one of about 55-60% of full-2-torsion curves whose class holds a weak curve (section 18.5). Class accounting; no generic or deployed curve is in the class.
